what_its_for: Atomoxetine is used to treat Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in children age 6 and older, teenagers, and adults. It helps improve attention, reduce impulsiveness, and control hyperactivity (being overly active). Unlike some ADHD medicines, it is NOT a stimulant and is not a controlled substance.
how_to_take: Take atomoxetine exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or snack. Swallow the capsule whole — do not open, crush, or chew it. If a capsule is accidentally opened and the powder touches your eyes, rinse them with water right away and call your doctor. Wash your hands if powder touches your skin.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over a few weeks to find the right amount for you. Most people take it once a day in the morning, or it may be split into two doses — one in the morning and one in the late afternoon or early evening. Do not take it too late in the day as it may make it harder to fall asleep. Always follow your doctor's specific dosing instructions and never change your dose without asking your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store atomoxetine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a local drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking atomoxetine if you are currently taking or have taken an MAO inhibitor (such as phenelzine, tranylcypromine, selegiline, or linezolid) in the past 14 days — this combination can cause a serious, life-threatening reaction. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do other dangerous activities until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some medicines can interact with atomoxetine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you or your child experience: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, new or worsening depression or anxiety, aggressive behavior or unusual mood changes, chest pain, shortness of breath, or fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting or feeling lightheaded when standing up, yellowing of the skin or eyes (signs of liver problems), painful or difficult urination, or numbness or tingling in fingers or toes. Also call your doctor if you notice slowed growth or weight loss in a child taking this medicine. This medicine has a warning about an increased risk of suicidal thoughts in children and teenagers — monitor closely, especially in the first few months.
when_it_works: Atomoxetine does not work right away like some other ADHD medicines. It may take 2 to 4 weeks before you start noticing improvement, and the full benefit may take up to 6 to 8 weeks. It is important to keep taking it every day even if you do not notice results right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Children under 6 years old: This medicine is NOT approved for children younger than 6. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine. It may not be safe during pregnancy, and it is not known if it passes into breast milk. Older adults: Use with caution — your doctor may start you on a lower dose. People with heart problems or high blood pressure: Tell your doctor before starting this medicine, as it can raise blood pressure and heart rate. People with liver problems: Your dose may need to be adjusted. People with certain eye problems (narrow-angle glaucoma): This medicine may not be safe for you — tell your doctor about any eye conditions.
